title: Statin adherence → cardiac admissions
teaser: The healthy-adherer effect nobody mentions; injury admissions as a check.
question: How much does sticking to your statin reduce cardiac hospital admissions over the next year?
ask: Finance wants one number for the adherence programme business case.
sme: the pharmacy benefits analytics lead at a regional health insurer

treatment.name: adherent
treatment.meaning: 1 = filled the statin for at least 80% of days in the first 6 months

outcome.name: cardiac_adm_12m
outcome.meaning: 1 = admitted for a cardiac event in the following 12 months

variables.name: admits_prior_yr
variables.meaning: hospital admissions in the year before the prescription

variables.name: flu_shot_prior_yr
variables.meaning: 1 = had a flu vaccination in the year before the prescription

hidden.name: U_health
hidden.label: health-conscious habits
hidden.why: People who take pills as prescribed also look after themselves in other ways.

hidden.name: U_frail
hidden.label: early frailty that makes people stop their pills

negative_control.name: injury_adm_12m
negative_control.meaning: 1 = admitted for an accidental injury in the following 12 months

notes.text: Taking the statin as prescribed is the member's own choice; there was no programme or outreach during this period.
Claims data are complete for everyone in the file.
Members often stop their statin when they start feeling unwell, but we have no record of how they were feeling.

traps.name: Healthy-adherer effect
traps.text: Adherent members are healthier in unrecorded ways; adjusted estimates overstate the benefit roughly twofold.

traps.name: Negative-control outcome
traps.text: Injury admissions can't be prevented by a statin but fall among adherent members: evidence of the bias.

traps.name: Sick-stopper effect, unrecorded
traps.text: Members who feel unwell stop taking pills and are admitted more; nothing recorded captures it.
